newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: First African peacekeepers arrive in Bangui.
newsitem.headline: First African peacekeepers arrive in Bangui.

text.p: A contigent of 58 Gabonese soldiers arrived in the Central African Republic's capital Bangui on Friday, the advance guard of a 500-strong African peacekeeping force to help police a peace deal.

State television reported that the contingent arrived on board a plane provided by former colonial power France, whose troops currently patrol the capital Bangui as a buffer between rival army factions.

The peace deal, brokered by Mali's former military leader Amadou Toumani Toure, was signed on January 25 and aims to end the impoverished nation's third army mutiny in under a year and associated ethnic bloodshed.
It envisages amnesties, restoration of constitutional legality under the democratic transition and a peacekeeping force with soldiers from Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon, Mali, Senegal and Togo.

President Ange-Felix Patasse named outgoing foreign minister Michel Gbezzera-Bria on Thursday to head a "Government of Action for the Defence of Democracy". He replaces Jean-Paul Ngoumpande and has yet to name a government.

Mutinies in April and May began over pay and conditions but turned into a campaign to oust Patasse, a northern civilian who won presidential elections in 1993. The latest mutiny began on November 15 and degenerated into ethnic feuding.
The presidents of Gabon, Chad, Mali and Burkina Faso launched the mediation process in December at the behest of a Franco-African summit.
